summary: Voice-note transcription now runs on a Cantonese-tuned whisper model by default, with the existing SenseVoice engine kept as a config-selectable backup.
details: The local STT service's default engine is now JackyHoCL whisper-large-v3-turbo-cantonese-noise-detection (transformers, on-box, fp32 CPU). In the 2026-09-15 A/B on real voice audio it was the only engine that kept both English entities (`RV`, `discord`) intact, and it emits Traditional Chinese with punctuation out of the box — where SenseVoice dropped letters, misheard `discord` as `discuss`, and emitted Simplified with no punctuation.

SenseVoiceSmall stays deployed as the backup: it is the latency floor (near-instant on short notes) and fails over with no new infrastructure. `[speech.stt] model = "sensevoice"` selects it; configs written before the `model` key existed keep loading and get the new default.
Audio still never leaves the box: both engines run inside the same private-network `stt` container, and the response shape Nora sees is unchanged.
limitations: The new default is heavier: roughly half real-time on CPU (a 21-second note takes ~10 seconds) versus SenseVoice's near-instant. The first container boot downloads ~3.2GB of weights from Hugging Face, so the first start is slow; the cache volume makes subsequent starts fast.
Transcription is mildly non-deterministic now — the model card's generation settings (temperature 0.3, top_p 0.5) imply sampling, so the same audio can transcribe slightly differently across calls.
